title: Ideal black-body spectrum
question: How do the wavelength curve, its peak, and total emitted power per area respond to thermodynamic temperature?
predictionPrompt: When thermodynamic temperature increases, predict whether the wavelength-form peak shifts shorter, shifts longer, or stays unchanged, and whether ideal radiant exitance follows the fourth power of the temperature ratio, follows it linearly, or stays unchanged.
sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
sourceLocator: OpenStax section 6.1; BIPM sections 2.2-2.3; CODATA radiation-constant entries
caveats: The activity fixes ideal spectral emissivity at 1 and does not model a material surface.
The generated curve is neither measured spectral data nor a color-appearance prediction.

numericalMethod.name: Bounded stable Planck wavelength evaluation
numericalMethod.description: Evaluates 2 to 256 positive logarithmically spaced wavelength samples using expm1 for exp(x)-1 and the limiting value zero above the finite exponential range; it rejects non-finite or negative output points.

modelComponents.label: Planck wavelength spectral radiance
modelComponents.description: Calculates ideal black-body spectral radiance B_lambda for positive wavelength and thermodynamic temperature.

attribution.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27
caveats: The component is the wavelength density B_lambda with ideal emissivity one.

modelComponents.label: Wien wavelength peak
modelComponents.description: Calculates lambda_max = b/T independently of the finite plotting interval.

attribution.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment
attribution.sourceLocator: OpenStax section 6.1; CODATA Wien wavelength displacement law constant
caveats: The peak is for wavelength spectral radiance, not frequency spectral radiance.

modelComponents.label: Stefan-Boltzmann radiant exitance
modelComponents.description: Calculates all-wavelength ideal radiant exitance M = sigma T^4 independently of the displayed interval.

attribution.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment
caveats: The total assumes hemispherical emission from an ideal surface with emissivity one.

assumptions: Thermodynamic temperature is positive, uniform, and represented by the selected input.
Spectral emissivity is exactly 1 at every wavelength in the activity.
The source is in thermal equilibrium and is represented by the ideal Planck model.
The sampled wavelength interval is a display bound, not the domain used to define the analytic all-wavelength total.
No atmosphere, line spectrum, detector response, uncertainty model, or color-matching function is included.
The spectrum is modeled output and is not loaded or measured data.

controls.label: Thermodynamic temperature
controls.description: Sets the uniform ideal-emitter temperature used by the Planck, Wien, and Stefan-Boltzmann calculations.
controls.playfulPrompt: Warm the ideal emitter and watch the peak move left while the total rises quickly.

controls.label: Minimum wavelength
controls.description: Sets the lower logarithmic-grid bound accepted by the engine; it must remain below the maximum wavelength.

controls.label: Maximum wavelength
controls.description: Sets the upper logarithmic-grid bound accepted by the engine; it must remain above the minimum wavelength.

controls.label: Series samples
controls.description: Sets the bounded integer number of logarithmic wavelength points evaluated by the engine.

presets.label: Room
presets.description: A 293.15 K room-temperature ideal black body.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Find its infrared peak without interpreting the curve as a room measurement.

presets.label: Human-ish
presets.description: A 310 K ideal black-body comparison, not a human emissivity model.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Compare the peak with the room preset while retaining the emissivity caveat.

presets.label: Incandescent
presets.description: A representative 2700 K hot-filament ideal black-body temperature, not a material-emissivity fit.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Compare its longer peak wavelength and lower total exitance with the Sun-scale preset.

presets.label: Sun photosphere
presets.description: Uses 5772 K as a conventional effective-temperature black-body comparison for the Sun.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Locate the wavelength-form peak, then identify which solar spectral features this smooth ideal curve cannot contain.

presets.label: Hot star
presets.description: A generic 10000 K hot-star ideal black-body comparison.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Track the shorter wavelength peak without treating the curve as a measured stellar spectrum.

outputSchema.label: Model temperature
outputSchema.description: Validated temperature input used by every model component.

outputSchema.label: Wien peak wavelength
outputSchema.description: Engine output b/T for the wavelength-form peak, independent of the sampled grid.

outputSchema.label: Ideal radiant exitance
outputSchema.description: Engine output sigma T^4 for analytic all-wavelength ideal radiant exitance.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render runs separately without pointwise ratios, merged curves, or residual claims when compatibility keys differ.

visualization.description: Plots the finite Planck wavelength series, marks the analytic Wien peak when it lies in the window, and presents the Stefan-Boltzmann total separately from the sampled curve.

alternatives.description: Reports temperature, fixed emissivity, wavelength interval, analytic peak, peak-window status, total exitance, and the modeled-data boundary.
Lists every sampled wavelength and spectral-radiance pair, followed by analytic peak and total fields.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render the completed bounded curve and markers immediately without animated drawing or peak movement.

finding.changed: At runtime, changing thermodynamic temperature is specified to reshape the finite ideal spectrum, move its analytic wavelength peak, and change total radiant exitance.
finding.cause: Planck's exponent contains inverse temperature, Wien's wavelength peak scales as 1/T, and Stefan-Boltzmann radiant exitance scales as T^4.
finding.equation: B_lambda = (2 h c^2/lambda^5)/expm1(h c/(lambda k_B T)); lambda_max = b/T; M = sigma T^4
assumptions: Engine wavelength bounds from 10^-9 m through 10^-2 m and at most 256 samples
No measured dataset, detector response, atmosphere, or color model
finding.establishes: For an evaluated run, the finite numerical outputs implied by the declared ideal model, constants, controls, bounds, and implementation revision.
finding.doesNotEstablish: A measured source spectrum, physical-source temperature, material emissivity, perceived color, empirical agreement, or validation of black-body theory.
finding.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment; tour-content-2026-07-26
finding.sourceLocator: Planck, Wien, and Stefan-Boltzmann laws; blackbody-spectrum numerical and provenance contract
caveats: The analytic total includes wavelengths outside the displayed interval.
The Sun-scale and incandescent-scale presets are illustrative model inputs, not measurements.
